description: EXPERIMENTAL and HARDWARE-UNTESTED: this recipe has never been run on a Spark here or anywhere in this fleet, and it will likely need platform work before it can start (see the platform gap below). GLM-5.3-Flash on three DGX Sparks with the TensorFold engine (exact decoding, custom CUDA kernels JIT-compiled on first start), tensor parallel over three ranks, one per Spark, with NCCL for every all-gather (the kit's three-Spark default; COMM=roce is a kit option this recipe does not offer). Platform gap, stated plainly: the kit needs a triangle of direct ConnectX-7 cables with one RoCE subnet per cable and a link between every pair of Sparks, and vonk-forge's fabric layer is two-node point to point today (runtime_fabric.rs binds one link and one GID, and recipe_operations.py hands every rank the master's fabric address), so a three-Spark run will likely need platform work first. The hardware sweep skips this recipe because the fleet has two Sparks. It is the two-Spark recipe's sibling: the same adapter, kit lock and Models (the kit's engine for more than two ranks comes from its patches 0066-0068, which the shared image already carries), with the kit's three-Spark defaults from its scripts/config.sh at the pinned commit: 8 concurrent requests (PARALLEL=8, the settings default here), a 64-row verify window (TF_GLM_MULTI_WINDOW=64), a host memory reserve of 19.6 GiB, TF_ROCE_MAX_KB=1024, a 32 GiB KV pool (TF_GLM_CACHE_GIB=32; the kit's measured pool is about 4M tokens), and the NCCL settings its three-Spark launcher sets (NCCL_CROSS_NIC=1, NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1, NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1, NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1). Serves MiaAI-Lab's EXL3 4 bpw TensorFold checkpoint (EXL3 routed experts, BF16 elsewhere; Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-4bpw-TensorFold at the revision the kit pins) with a 1,048,576-token window, DFlash2 and copy drafts, 4-bit dense weights, image and video input (up to 50 images and 4 videos a request, each picture keeping its size across a chat), a keep-alive comment on a silent stream every 15 s, tool calling (a call is sent whole, never cut off) and structured outputs, smooth token streaming, earlier turns' reasoning kept in the prompt, a default reply budget of 32,768 tokens for requests that set none, and room for 32 kept prompt states. Based on MiaAI-Lab's TensorFold kit at commit bf5f9452 (v1.10 plus later commits, Apache-2.0) on TensorFold v0.6.0 (Apache-2.0; code written before 0.6.0 keeps its MIT notice) with her 123 patches, applied at fuzz 0; the recipe runs the same published image as the two-Spark one (Mia's v0.6.0-789e8f3bdfa2, sha256:99fe7496d7002fd8f2ca3b1beb0aa07513835cd09989ca657b65875d60f69956) and does not rebuild it from the patches. Upstream's three-Spark figures, all unmeasured here: with 8 requests at once 166.0 tok/s prose and 211.5 code aggregate (121.8 and 165.3 at 4), 65.7 tok/s prose for one request, about 2,000 tok/s prefill; rank 0 had 14.4 GiB free idle and 11.5 GiB at its lowest under a 195k-token prompt (ranks 1 and 2: 27.6 / 21.1 GiB). The memory envelope below reuses the two-Spark recipe's engine figure (rank 0 grown by the 0.65 GiB of vision workspace the kit now sets aside) with this recipe's larger reserve and is an estimate. Licences, for information: the quantization is Apache-2.0 per the kit's NOTICE, with Z.AI's MIT licence kept for the base model (the pinned checkpoint revision's own LICENSE and card still carry Z.AI's MIT text; the relicensing is a later upstream commit that changes no weights); the DFlash2 drafter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial) and is not used with the MTP drafter option. Thinking is on by default (the chat template's default) and is chosen per request: a request can set reasoning_effort or chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking, and reasoning comes back in reasoning_content.
title: GLM 5.3 Flash EXL3 DFlash2 TensorFold three Sparks
